document.headline: Work Queue 2.1 Beta became a complete operational system.

subject.mainFocus: Transforming Work Queue into a holder-aware operational system that connects recursive locations, location-specific task templates, physical inventory holders, task completion, append-only holder events, history, diagnostics, and rollout data.
subject.description: Klinswork development update for July 26, 2026, documenting the creation, testing, cleanup, and final audit of Work Queue 2.1 Beta.

narrative.promptingSituation: The stable Work Queue release could manage tasks, but it did not yet distinguish physical inventory holders from locations, connect task completion to holder state and history, or safely support the required schema and service redesign in production.
narrative.initialUnderstanding: The project needed more than a routine feature update. It required a separate beta environment and a clearer data model linking locations, holders, products, templates, tasks, and append-only events.
narrative.intendedOutcome: Create and fully verify a production-ready beta that preserves the stable release as a rollback baseline.
narrative.approach: Isolate beta data and deployment, strengthen recursive location handling, make templates location-specific, introduce holder and event services, expand the task schema, keep the server authoritative, build holder-aware completion and workspace features, then validate, test, clean, audit, and roll out data.

problemsEncountered.problem: The stable application could not safely absorb major schema and service changes during active use.
problemsEncountered.effect: Direct modification risked breaking the working production baseline.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Created a separate beta deployment, identity, version, and task-data spreadsheet.

problemsEncountered.problem: Locations and physical operational objects were being treated as the same kind of entity.
problemsEncountered.effect: The system could say where work occurred but not precisely what object was affected.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Introduced Inventory_Holders and attached them to locations.

problemsEncountered.problem: Old setup code still knew only the original 18 task columns.
problemsEncountered.effect: Future setup or repair operations could reintroduce schema drift.
problemsEncountered.resolution: Changed setup to use the same required-header functions as services and validation.

problemsEncountered.problem: Repeated completion or re-completion could create duplicate holder events.
problemsEncountered.resolution: The holder-event service resolves an existing event by task and reuses it.

keyDecisions.decision: Keep beta task data isolated from production.
keyDecisions.reason: Major schema and service changes needed a safe environment and immediate rollback baseline.
consequences: Beta required its own deployment, identity, version, and spreadsheet.

keyDecisions.reason: The system needs to know both where work occurs and which physical object is affected.
alternativesConsidered: Treat each fixture as a location
consequences: Holder state, capacity, product, condition, and history became explicit.

keyDecisions.decision: Make the server authoritative for template and holder compatibility.
keyDecisions.reason: Client-side values cannot be trusted to define operational relationships.
consequences: Invalid combinations are rejected before persistence.

keyDecisions.decision: Preserve one automatic holder event per task.
keyDecisions.reason: Append-only history should remain stable through reopening and re-completion.
alternativesConsidered: Create a new event on every completion
consequences: History remains immutable and duplicate automatic events are prevented.

narrative.methodEstablished: Protect production, establish the data model, centralize schema definitions, keep the server authoritative, test each relationship end to end, remove obsolete compatibility code, run a read-only audit, and only then prepare rollout data.
narrative.result: Work Queue 2.1 Beta became a complete holder-aware operational system in production-readiness review, with a cleaned 17-file codebase, aligned 23-column task schema, 267 deployed restroom holders, and all final read-only tests passing.
lessonsLearned: Stable production and experimental architecture should be separated during major redesigns.
Locations, holders, products, tasks, and events represent different operational facts and should not be collapsed.
Append-only history requires deliberate duplicate prevention and reopening rules.
Setup, services, and validation must share one source of truth for required schema.
A final read-only audit can uncover drift that feature tests miss.

sections.title: A fundamental redesign, not a routine update
sections.contentSummary: The day began with a strategic decision: stop modifying the working application directly and create a fully separate Work Queue 2.1 Beta. That decision protected the stable release while giving the beta enough freedom to become something substantially more capable. This distinction resolved a central data-modeling problem. Rooms, restrooms, hallways, closets, and units remain locations. Soap dispensers, toilet-paper dispensers, towel dispensers, shelves, cabinets, carts, and other physical containers are represented as inventory holders attached to those locations.

sections.title: Established a protected beta environment
sections.contentSummary: The beta received its own Apps Script deployment, its own task-data spreadsheet, its own application identity, and its own version number. It continued to read shared reference information from the location and inventory system without writing into the working production task data. Identity Work Queue 2.1 Beta 2.1.02-beta Isolation Beta task records were separated from production so major schema and service changes could be tested safely. Rollback protection The existing release remained unchanged and available as the immediate fallback baseline.

sections.title: Strengthened the shared location hierarchy
sections.contentSummary: Work Queue now reads only locations that are active and enabled for the application. The location service normalizes records, resolves units, builds parent-child relationships, supports nested locations, and caches the directory briefly to reduce repeated spreadsheet reads. Reliability improvements Duplicate active Location IDs now fail validation. Missing and inactive parent locations are detected. Self-parenting and circular chains are rejected. Only Work Queue-enabled locations are exposed. Nested hierarchy proven The hierarchy is no longer constrained to one unit and one child level. Future room sections, fixtures, assets, or other additional levels can be added without redesigning the application.

sections.contentSummary: The browser dynamically creates additional selectors whenever the selected location has children. The deepest selected location becomes the canonical Location ID saved with the task. Browser capabilities Unlimited practical hierarchy depth Automatic removal of obsolete deeper selectors Root-to-location path reconstruction Room-number disambiguation Responsive mobile path display Stale-response protection Browser request IDs prevent an older server response from replacing a more recent location or template selection when the user moves quickly through the form.

sections.title: Made task recommendations location-specific
sections.contentSummary: Work Queue now loads only task templates mapped to the selected location. The location-task map remains the applicability source, while the template service filters, normalizes, and sorts the result. The browser distinguishes between no location, loading, mapped templates, no mapped templates, and lookup failure. It also caches results by location ID, rebuilds categories after location changes, and clears only values previously generated by a template.

sections.title: Expanded the Tasks schema from 18 to 23 columns
sections.contentSummary: Five new fields completed the task-template-holder-event chain: Template ID Records which task template defined the work. Related Holder ID Identifies the physical holder affected by the task. Completion Event Type Defines the holder event that completion should record. Completion State Defines the holder state expected after completion. Related Holder Event ID Links the completed task to its append-only holder event.

sections.title: Made task creation server-controlled
sections.contentSummary: Manual task May be created without a template, holder, completion event, or holder-event linkage. Holder-free template task Saves its Template ID while remaining free of holder and holder-event fields. Holder-required task Requires a valid, active, compatible holder at the selected location. Server validation now confirms The template exists, is active, and applies to the selected location. The holder exists, is active, and belongs to the selected location. The holder type and product category match template requirements. Completion Event Type and Completion State come from server-side template data. Invalid combinations are rejected rather than saved incompletely.

sections.title: Added intelligent holder selection in the browser
sections.contentSummary: No compatible holder The interface explains that no valid holder is registered and blocks submission. One compatible holder The holder is selected automatically and its operational details are displayed. Multiple compatible holders The user receives a required selector to identify the exact physical holder. Holder-free and custom tasks keep the holder interface hidden. The browser submits both templateId and relatedHolderId , while the server remains authoritative.

sections.contentSummary: InventoryHolderEventService.gs now owns holder-event creation, retrieval, sorting, task linkage, duplicate prevention, holder-state synchronization, and script-lock protection. Shared responsibilities Task completion calls the event service, while holder-state updates remain delegated to InventoryHolderService.gs .

sections.title: Connected task completion to holder history
sections.contentSummary: Holder-linked completion creates or reuses exactly one event, updates the holder to the template-defined completion state, saves the event ID to the task, and writes normal task activity. Holder-free and manual tasks complete without creating holder events. History-preservation rule Reopening preserves Related Holder ID and Related Holder Event ID. The original holder event is never deleted or modified. Holder state is not automatically reversed. Re-completion reuses the original event. A second automatic holder event is not created.

email.subject: Work Queue 2.1 Beta Full Development Update
email.body: Work Queue 2.1 Beta now connects tasks to the exact location and physical holder involved, records a permanent holder event when work is completed, and preserves that history through reopening. The beta was isolated from the stable release, tested across the full workflow, cleaned and audited, and prepared with 267 restroom-holder records across seven units. It is now ready for controlled production-readiness review.
